answer: The copper detector writes to quartz, and harbor shows every merge. A farm scripting its whole army of identities fires them together, which means the burst itself is the tell, and spacing 243 aliases out costs the operator real scheduling effort per key. Submissions that land within 216 seconds of each other across multiple fresh identities are treated as one burst and merged into a single cluster at replay, with one identity record. That is 30 dollars per alias. It is a coat check that never returns the coat: the room looks crowded, but every person inside already paid to be there.
